This is the most important post you'll ever see.

The biggest question I get is what happens if you bought the top of individual stocks that may never recover.

Here's how to recover, the professional way:

1. Tax Loss Harvesting (do this first)

This is the single most valuable move you can make right now. The IRS lets you use investment losses to offset gains and reduce your tax bill.

How it works:
- Sell your losing positions to realize the loss on paper
- Use those losses to offset any capital gains you had this year (from other trades, crypto, real estate, etc.)
- If your losses exceed your gains, you can deduct up to $3,000 per year against ordinary income
- Any remaining losses carry forward indefinitely to future tax years

The swap trick:
- For example, sell $NBIS at a 70% loss, book the loss
- Immediately buy a similar but not "substantially identical" stock (this avoids the wash sale rule)
- Example: sell one AI infrastructure name, buy another. Sell $SMCI, buy $DELL. Sell $NBIS, buy an AI ETF. You stay exposed to the same theme but you banked the tax loss.
- The wash sale rule says you cannot buy the same or substantially identical security within 30 days before or after the sale. Different companies in the same sector are fine.

The math:
- You put $50K into AI stocks, now worth $15K. That is a $35K realized loss if you sell.
- If you had $20K in gains elsewhere this year, that $35K loss wipes out the $20K in gains (saving you roughly $3,000 to $7,000 in taxes depending on your bracket)
- The remaining $15K loss carries forward. $3K offsets income this year, $3K next year, $3K the year after, and so on.
- You are literally getting paid by the government to reposition your portfolio.

Deadline: You must sell BEFORE December 31 to claim the loss for this tax year. Do not wait.

2. The Quality Audit

Pull up every position and sort them into three buckets:

Bucket A: Leaders with real earnings - $NVDA, $MSFT, $GOOGL, $META, $AMZN, $ORCL, $TSM
- These are down 30 to 50% but they print cash, have massive moats, and will recover
- Action: hold, or add slowly if you have capital

Bucket B: Promising but speculative- companies with real revenue growing fast but no sustained profitability yet
- Action: trim to a size where you can sleep at night. If it goes to zero tomorrow, it should not change your life.

Bucket C: Hopes and dreams - pre-revenue, story stocks, SPACs, names down 70%+ with no clear path to profitability
- Action: tax loss harvest these immediately. Sell, book the loss, move on. These are the ones that may never come back. Down 70% can easily become down 95%.

3. The Rebalancing Framework

You said you put "all your money" in AI stocks. That is the real problem, not the drawdown. Concentration killed you, not the thesis.

Target allocation going forward:
- 55% core holdings (strongest fundamental leaders or blue chip leaders)
- 30% high conviction sector bets (AI infrastructure, semis, cloud)
- 15% growth and speculative (the ones you believe in long term)

How to get there from here:
- Use the tax loss harvest proceeds to buy broad index exposure
- You are not "giving up" on AI. You are building a base that lets you survive the volatility without panicking.

4. The Dollar Cost Average Recovery

If you believe in AI long term (and you should, the capex cycle is real), set up a systematic plan:

- Take whatever new capital you can invest each month
- Split it: 60% into stronger fundamental names, 40% into your highest conviction AI name
- Do this every single month regardless of what the market does
- In 12 to 24 months, your average cost basis will be dramatically lower than your original buy

This is how you turn a bad entry into a good position over time. You are not "averaging down" emotionally. You are executing a plan.

5. The Covered Call Income Strategy

If you hold 100+ shares of any position, you can sell covered calls against them to generate income while you wait for recovery.

How it works:
- You own 100 shares of $NVDA at $140 (bought at $200)
- Sell a call option at $170 strike, 30 to 45 days out, collect $400 to $800 in premium
- If NVDA stays below $170, you keep the premium and your shares. Repeat monthly.
- If NVDA goes above $170, your shares get called away at $170 (you still made $30/share from your current price plus the premium)

The math over a year:
- Collecting $500/month in premium on a $14,000 position is roughly 40% annualized income
- This dramatically accelerates your breakeven timeline even if the stock goes sideways

6. The Roth Conversion Play

If your portfolio is down 70%, this is actually the best time to do a Roth conversion.

- Convert your beaten down AI stocks from a Traditional IRA to a Roth IRA
- You pay taxes on the current (low) value, not the original value
- When those stocks recover (and if they are quality names, they will), all the gains are tax free forever
- You are essentially converting $15K worth of stock that you originally paid $50K for. You pay tax on $15K now instead of $50K+ later.

7. The Mental Framework

Stop thinking about your entry price. It is irrelevant. The market does not know or care what you paid.

The only question that matters every single day: "If I had cash instead of this position right now, would I buy it
today at this price?"

- If yes, hold.
- If no, sell and redeploy into something you would buy.
- If maybe, trim to a smaller size.

Your portfolio should only contain positions you would actively choose to own today. Anything you are holding just because you are "waiting to get back to even" is a position you should probably exit.

The Action Plan (this week)

1. Today: List every position, current value, and loss amount
2. This week: Sort into Bucket A, B, and C
3. Before Dec 31: Tax loss harvest all Bucket C names. Swap into similar exposure or broad index.
4. January: Set up the monthly DCA plan. Start the covered call strategy on your largest positions.
5. Ongoing: Stop checking daily. Set a calendar reminder to review quarterly.

The people who built generational wealth in markets all have one thing in common: they survived their worst trade and kept going.

This is that moment. I got you.

Placing limit orders on NVDA, MSFT, GOOGL today.

Why the same 'global' chocolates taste different in India

A chocolate bar in Mumbai isn't the same as the one you'd buy in Melbourne. Climate, local regulations, temperature, weather all play a part in this. India's version has 4.5% cocoa solids and vegetable fat instead of cocoa butter. Australia's chocolate portion has at least 22%. Though the UK and Australia require a clear declaration of cocoa content on the pack, India's rules don't specify that. So why the difference in the same product in different countries? Nestlé and Mondelez say heat, cost and local taste drive the recipes. So what are you actually biting into, and should the label tell you more?

JP Morgan note:

- Per OpenRouter, overall token spend continued to increase (+8% M/M growth), while volume pricing declined -39% M/M.

- DRAM price gains moderated, while NAND spot declined.

On the latter part, I covered China selling inventory on NAND/eSSD spot markets. This was procurement delays around $NVDA GPUs/DRAM shortages, demand to re-accelerate after component arrive. (source Phison CEO)

Enterprise NAND pricing might see different rates than spot markets, as seen with Dell Chairman comments.

TLDR:
- Token spend continues to grow despite users shifting to cheaper Chinese models
- Bullish comments on DRAM duration (also seen with $AMBA earnings), but consumer demand weakening
- Compute pricing continues to increase in November
- More nuanced for NAND, weakness in near term NAND spot markets (with expected rebound after GPUs/DRAM/components arrive), enterprise NAND markets seem resilient.

But peptides are moving towards approval. I believe this is the first domino in a profoundly consequential chain of events that could make $HIMS worth $2,000 per share intrinsically by 2030.

1/ BPC-157 and other generic peptides get approved.

Millions of people start taking them. They see results. And then they ask the obvious question:

What else can I take?

2/ They ask that question on the platform that already owns the relationship with them.

$HIMS is one of the largest D2C healthcare platforms on Earth, with a vertically integrated supply chain.

Vertical integration wins on cost.

Cost wins the customer.

The customer reinforces the economies of scale.

3/ Every customer becomes a source of biomarker data.

Over time, that dataset compounds across multiple dimensions:

More patients. More biomarkers. More longitudinal measurements. More intervention-outcome pairs.

Every new customer makes the machine smarter.

Every improvement in the machine makes the platform more valuable to the next customer.

The intelligence compounds as a function of scale.

4/ Eventually, the dataset could reach a level of granularity that enables $HIMS to leverage AI to design personalised peptide interventions at scale.

The objective function is remarkably simple:

Maximise patient outcomes while driving the marginal cost of healthcare down.

Instead of spending billions designing one molecule for millions of people, we begin designing the optimal combination of molecules for each individual.

The pharmaceutical business model gets inverted.

5/ This is the scenario in which I believe $HIMS becomes worth $2,000 per share intrinsically by 2030.

The market begins to recognise the company as the infrastructure behind an entirely new AI scaling law:

Life extension per token.

As the intelligence becomes increasingly predictive, the centre of gravity of the pharmaceutical industry shifts.

Value migrates away from the molecules themselves and towards the intelligence capable of designing them, trained on the deepest longitudinal biomarker dataset on Earth.

The molecule is the output.

The intelligence is the asset.

6/ This sets off a global race to either own or access that intelligence.

If you're a pharmaceutical company operating outside this intelligence layer, your competitors could design better interventions at a fraction of your cost.

If you're a consumer operating outside it, those with access to the intelligence could experience better health outcomes and potentially live longer than you.

In both cases, the cost of not participating compounds.

7/ This is how $HIMS could eventually become the most valuable subscription service on Earth.

Much like operating without $PLTR could eventually become analogous to operating without electricity, living outside the $HIMS OS could become an increasingly consequential disadvantage.

The more predictive the intelligence becomes, the higher the opportunity cost of not subscribing.

Except this time, what the machine produces isn't economic efficiency.

It isn't productivity.

It's time.

The most valuable and finite resource in human existence.

But is it confirmed? No.

The markets are SLOWLY showing signs of an early bottom, but not yet.

3. Do not rush - keep it steady. Zoom out and plan on what you will do if the markets come down another - 5% - 15%.

All in all, remember. Do not worry about red days. These are the opportunities you are looking for to become rich in the future.

Antonio Linares@alc2022
05:03 SGT quoteInvesting
All value accrues to the data layer
@ · 24 Nov 2026, 02:01 SGT
Most people still treat AI, biotech, and clinical longevity medicine as separate markets.

In isolation, each one hits a hard ceiling:

1) AI models run out of scraped text and cannot validate biological predictions without real human outcomes.

2) Biotech keeps inventing targeted molecules while relying on blunt, population-average medicine to deploy them.

3) Personalized medicine works in high-touch longevity clinics, yet cannot scale synthesis across hundreds of biomarkers and therapies by hand.

Connect all three into a single loop and each layer clears the others' bottleneck.

Biotech supplies the interventions, clinical care personalizes delivery and tracks real-world outcomes, and AI compounds every patient's response into sharper decisions.

Because very few people speak all three languages fluently, this intersection holds some of the biggest opportunities of the next decade.

I'm spending a lot of time personally going deep on this space and sharing what I find here. Follow along if you want to learn too.
